articles.title: Why Did Alphabet (GOOGL) Shares Fall After Its $500 Billion Value Wipeout?
articles.summary: Alphabet (NasdaqGS: GOOGL) shed about US$500b in market value after its Q3 update, with the stock falling over 12%. Management reported slower-than-expected...
articles.body:
Alphabet (NasdaqGS: GOOGL) shed about US$500b in market value after its Q3 update, with the stock falling over 12%.

Management reported slower-than-expected trends in core search and advertising activity, which weighed heavily on investor sentiment.

The group also disclosed substantial negative free cash flow tied to heavy AI and data center spending during the quarter.

Fresh concern over the financial impact of Alphabet's historic US$500b market cap drop fits into broader themes this research has been tracking. Check out 4 other big wins that Alphabet investors should know about.

Alphabet is far from the only large platform pouring capital into AI infrastructure, so it is worth scanning peers exposed to similar build outs through 54 AI infrastructure stocks .

Alphabet runs global platforms like Search, YouTube and Android across the US, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, the Asia Pacific, Canada and Latin America, so its heavy AI and data center outlay directly affects how these products evolve and compete within interactive media and services.

Why did Alphabet lose about US$500b in value on one earnings print?

The share price reaction reflects investors focusing on the mix, not just the size, of Alphabet's results. Q3 showed sales of US$127.6b, but net income for the quarter fell to US$26.5b, and heavy AI and data center spending pushed free cash flow into a US$9.1b loss, which sharpened concern about cash generation.

Does this change the Alphabet Narrative around AI driven growth?

The Narrative still leans on AI powered Search, YouTube and an AI heavy Google Cloud backlog to support long term growth. However, this quarter highlights the key risk that large AI capex can pressure free cash flow if sub two year server paybacks and TPU monetization arrive more slowly than expected.

What should investors watch next to judge whether Alphabet's AI spend is working?

The cleanest near term gauge is whether future quarters show Google Cloud and AI related revenues scaling faster than AI capex. Management may also focus on disclosing improving free cash flow alongside any continued ramp in data center investment, especially through 2027 when more TPU system revenue is scheduled to be recognized.

articles.title: Why Affluent Investors Over 60 Are Emptying the Traditional 401(k) First and Leaving the Roth to Their Kids
articles.summary: The account you plan to leave your kids could quietly hand the IRS a larger cut than if you spent it yourself, and the math behind why surprises most people...
articles.body:
Wealthy retirees spend traditional 401(k) funds first so high-earning heirs inherit tax-free Roth dollars instead of paying 32% on forced distributions.

A married couple can withdraw up to roughly $218,000 before triggering Medicare IRMAA surcharges, adding about $2,297 yearly in extra premiums.

Taking large traditional withdrawals before claiming Social Security avoids pushing up to 85% of benefits into taxable income, which can spike effective rates to 41%.

The biggest 401k decisions tend to get made once and never revisited: when to roll it over, what to hold inside it, and when to start taking money out. That is exactly what the report: 401k & IRA Tips and Answers was created to address, and it is free today. Read more here . (Sponsor)

Picture a hypothetical married 64-year-old with $950,000 in a traditional 401(k) and $250,000 in Roth savings. His plan is to pay for retirement mostly from the pretax account and leave the Roth to his two children, who both earn high salaries.

More wealthy retirees choose this withdrawal order on purpose. They spend taxed money at their own bracket. They leave behind the money that comes out tax-free, so their heirs never pay tax on it at their higher rates.

Why a Roth Dollar Is Worth More to a High-Earning Heir

Traditional 401(k) withdrawals are subject to ordinary income tax rates. Qualified Roth withdrawals carry no federal income tax. Say you take a $250,000 traditional distribution taxed at an assumed 24%. The federal bill is $60,000, which leaves $190,000. The same amount from a qualified Roth comes whole.

Now hand that money to a child in the middle of a peak-earning career. Most non-spouse heirs have to empty an inherited account by the end of the 10th year after death. Traditional money stacked on top of a large salary could be taxed at 32%. On that same $250,000, the tax comes to $80,000. The Roth also has no required withdrawals while the owner is alive, so it can keep growing untouched for decades.

articles.title: Compras agrícolas da China nos EUA vão ao menor nível em 7 anos  | G1
articles.standfirst: Pequim prometeu comprar ao menos US$ 17 bilhões por ano em produtos agrícolas americanos, fora a soja; demanda fraca e concorrência dificultam avanço das compras.
articles.summary: Pequim prometeu comprar ao menos US$ 17 bilhões por ano em produtos agrícolas americanos, fora a soja; demanda fraca e concorrência dificultam avanço das compras.
articles.body:
Mais de 60% do volume de soja exportado de MT vai para a China — Foto: Reprodução/TVCA

As compras chinesas de produtos agrícolas dos Estados Unidos , excluindo a soja, caminham para o menor nível em sete anos, apesar do compromisso de Pequim de adquirir ao menos US$ 17 bilhões (R$ 92,16 bilhões) por ano em mercadorias do setor americano.

Entre janeiro e setembro, a China comprou US$ 7,2 bilhões (R$ 39,03 bilhões) em outros produtos agrícolas americanos, de carnes a milho, o menor valor para o período desde 2019, auge da primeira guerra comercial entre os dois países.

A soja faz parte de um compromisso separado, e a China caminha para cumprir a meta prevista para o produto.

Ainda não está claro, porém, se Pequim está descumprindo o acordo sobre os demais produtos. A Casa Branca não informou se o prazo começou a contar após o anúncio de maio ou se terá início apenas quando forem concluídos os cortes de tarifas propostos pela China, o que ainda não ocorreu.

O ritmo lento das compras aumenta as dúvidas sobre uma recuperação das importações ainda neste ano e frustra agricultores americanos, que também enfrentam combustíveis mais caros.

A questão ganhou peso político às vésperas das eleições de meio de mandato desta terça-feira (3), com democratas tentando conquistar eleitores de regiões agrícolas tradicionalmente ligados ao Partido Republicano, do presidente Donald Trump .

“Nossos produtores são patriotas, mas há muitos silos cheios de grãos e, certamente, uma vontade de ver esse comércio acontecer”, afirmou Tim Lust, diretor-executivo da National Sorghum Producers, entidade que representa produtores de sorgo. “A soja está sendo negociada, mas outras commodities não.”

O Departamento de Agricultura dos EUA encaminhou ao Escritório do Representante Comercial dos EUA (USTR) as perguntas sobre como a meta proporcional para 2026 será calculada. O USTR, a Casa Branca e o Ministério do Comércio da China não responderam aos pedidos de comentário.

Demanda fraca e concorrência dificultam exportações dos EUA

Mesmo que as compras aumentem, analistas avaliam que será difícil atingir a meta diante da demanda fraca na China e da concorrência de outros fornecedores. Para alcançar o valor previsto, Pequim provavelmente terá de mobilizar empresas estatais para ampliar as aquisições.

O milho é um exemplo. Em 2021, no pico das compras, a China importou US$ 5,6 bilhões (R$ 30,4 bilhões) do grão americano, o equivalente a quase 20 milhões de toneladas.

No mês passado, a COFCO Futures, corretora ligada a uma estatal chinesa, afirmou que o milho dos EUA não estava competitivo, em parte por causa da ampla oferta doméstica. A empresa projetou importações de cerca de 900 mil toneladas do produto americano na safra 2026/27, iniciada em setembro.

As exportações americanas de sorgo para a China também perderam espaço. Em 2021, elas atingiram 6,5 milhões de toneladas, no valor de US$ 2,1 bilhões (R$ 11,4 bilhões), mas agora enfrentam a concorrência do Brasil, que obteve acesso ao mercado chinês em setembro de 2025.

Neste ano, o Brasil já enviou 1,7 milhão de toneladas de sorgo à China, com quase 1 milhão de toneladas adicionais previstas para embarque, segundo Eduardo Vanin, estrategista sênior de agricultura da Marex.

Os EUA, por sua vez, exportaram cerca de 3,7 milhões de toneladas para a China até o fim de agosto, segundo dados do governo americano. O volume supera o registrado no ano anterior, quando o comércio estagnou em meio às tensões entre os dois países. Nos últimos quatro meses, porém, as vendas praticamente pararam.

As carnes americanas enfrentam obstáculos semelhantes. A China tem oferta abundante de carne suína e de frango, enquanto a carne bovina dos EUA está mais cara devido à redução dos rebanhos no país.

A carne bovina também enfrenta barreiras regulatórias. Em maio, a China renovou as licenças de exportação de mais de 400 frigoríficos americanos, mas cerca de metade da capacidade de abate de gado de corte dos EUA continua sem autorização para vender ao mercado chinês, segundo a Federação de Exportação de Carnes dos EUA.

Alguns frigoríficos foram barrados depois que autoridades chinesas afirmaram ter encontrado resíduos de substâncias que não são aprovadas no país, disse Joe Schuele, porta-voz da entidade.

Diante dessas restrições, analistas avaliam que Pequim provavelmente precisará recorrer a empresas estatais para alcançar a meta de US$ 17 bilhões, como já vem fazendo com a soja. A decisão, segundo eles, dependerá em última instância de uma escolha política.

“Muito disso parece depender de até que ponto a China recorrerá às empresas estatais para fazer essas compras”, afirmou Darin Friedrichs, cofundador da Sitonia Consulting, empresa de inteligência do mercado agrícola especializada na China.

“É difícil chegar a US$ 17 bilhões em produtos que não sejam soja sem compras direcionadas e realizadas fora das condições normais de mercado.”

articles.title: China's 3 biggest airlines slip into losses as jet fuel prices more than double
articles.summary: China's three biggest airlines are heading towards another year of losses after reporting a sharp deterioration in their third-quarter financial
articles.body: China's three biggest airlines are heading towards another year of losses after reporting a sharp deterioration in their third-quarter financial performance, with soaring jet fuel prices, weak domestic airfares and typhoon-related disruptions weighing on earnings during the peak travel season.Air China and China eastern airlines are on course to record their seventh consecutive annual net loss since the Covid-19 pandemic, according to analyst estimates compiled by LSEG. China Southern Airlines, which returned to profitability in 2025 for the first time since 2019, is also expected to slip back into the red.Air China's third-quarter net profit dropped 92.6% year-on-year to 270.6 million yuan ($40.62 million). China Eastern reported a quarterly net profit of 64 million yuan, marking a 98.2% decline from the corresponding period last year.China southern, meanwhile, posted a net loss of 609 million yuan for the July-September quarter, compared with a profit of 3.84 billion yuan a year earlier.All three carriers recorded losses during the first nine months of 2026, reversing the profits they had reported over the same period in 2025.Rising fuel costs weigh on earningsThe July-September period, which coincides with China's busy summer travel season, is traditionally the most profitable quarter for the country's airlines. However, the carriers said a steep increase in jet fuel prices had adversely affected their financial results.Jet fuel prices have more than doubled since the US and Israel launched a military campaign against Iran in late February. Chinese airlines, which hedge a much smaller proportion of their fuel requirements than several Asian and European counterparts, are particularly exposed to fluctuations in oil prices.Intense competition keeps fares under pressureDomestic airfares also remained weak during the quarter amid stiff competition from other airlines and high-speed rail services.Huatai Securities estimated that air china's yields, an indicator of average fares, declined 5% during the period, making it difficult for the carrier to offset higher fuel expenses.Nathan Gee, head of asia-pacific transport research at BofA Global Research, said Chinese airlines were likely to remain loss-making in the seasonally weaker fourth quarter because of elevated jet fuel costs.He noted that third-quarter earnings had been marginally better than already subdued market expectations. Industry checks indicated that domestic fares had risen at double-digit rates year-on-year following the October Golden Week holiday, as airlines restrained capacity.However, Gee said fuel costs continued to be the biggest challenge, adding that airline margins remained under severe pressure from expensive jet fuel and subdued consumer demand.Airlines are seeking to increase the number of flying hours per aircraft to manage expenses, but opportunities for significant cost reductions remain limited, he said.Shares of Air China, China eastern and China southern have fallen 38%, 46% and 39%, respectively, so far this year.You use AI every day. articles.title: Reliance shares surge over 7%, eye best single-day gain since January 2024: What's driving the rally?
articles.summary: Shares of Reliance Industries surged over 7 per cent in early trade on Monday after the company reported a record quarterly profit for July-September.
articles.body: Shares of Reliance Industries surged over 7 per cent in early trade on Monday after the company reported a record quarterly profit for July-September. The stock jumped 7.12 per cent to Rs 1,246.45 on the BSE and 6.79 per cent to Rs 1,244 on the NSE. The rally added Rs 1,00,208.45 crore to the company's market capitalisation, taking it to Rs 16.74 lakh crore.The gains followed Reliance's record September-quarter performance, with consolidated profit, including the share of associates and joint ventures, rising 33.8 per cent year-on-year to Rs 29,550 crore. Net profit attributable to owners of the company increased 40 per cent to Rs 25,548 crore. Consolidated revenue rose 27.8 per cent to Rs 3.62 lakh crore, while EBITDA climbed 23.9 per cent to a record Rs 62,409 crore.The oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business was the biggest driver of the performance. Its segment EBITDA jumped 67.9 per cent to Rs 25,203 crore, while revenue increased 44.2 per cent to Rs 2.32 lakh crore. Stronger transportation fuel refining margins and improved petrochemical margins amid global supply disruptions supported the recovery.The rally in Reliance also lifted the broader market. At 10.24 am, the BSE Sensex was up 935.82 points at 75,390.02, while the NSE Nifty had gained 248.15 points to 23,300.05.Jefferies said O2C “hit the bullseye”, citing record crude processing, flexible sourcing and a shift towards higher-value fuel exports that helped Reliance benefit from favourable refining conditions. The brokerage raised its earnings forecasts following the stronger-than-expected results.Emkay Global also pointed to the sharp recovery in O2C and improving profitability at Jio as key drivers of the earnings beat. It raised its estimates and maintained that the stock's valuation remained attractive.Retail continued to be the softer part of the business. Reliance Retail's gross revenue rose 6.4 per cent to Rs 91,716 crore, but EBITDA before a one-time impairment charge declined 8.6 per cent to Rs 6,228 crore. Investments in digital commerce, higher input costs and the shift of major festivals to the December quarter weighed on performance. JioMart, however, recorded 42 per cent revenue growth.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market and other asset classes given by experts are their own. articles.title: India's RE policies a role model for emerging economies: Analysis
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: As India looks to attract international investment and deepen cooperation in clean energy, green hydrogen, storage and manufacturing at the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: As India looks to attract international investment and deepen cooperation in clean energy, green hydrogen, storage and manufacturing at the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo (BRESE), a new international analysis has described the country as a “role model” in developing its renewable power sector, crediting its policy and regulatory measures for addressing investment risks and creating an environment conducive to private capital.The assessment comes at a time when India is looking to mobilise around $220 billion in investment between 2027 and 2030 to expand renewable energy capacity, manufacturing, transmission infrastructure and energy storage as it works towards its target of 500 GW of installed non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030. Govt has already secured $64 billion in private investment between June 2024 and June 2026, including $6.2 billion in foreign direct investment, MNRE secretary Santosh Sarangi told reporters earlier this week.The recent analysis by Zero Carbon Analytics, titled Emerging market financing for renewables, said India had adopted a holistic approach to addressing risks related to project development, construction and market access, describing the country as “a renewables powerhouse built on enabling policies”.The report said India's long-term target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030, backed by an annual bidding trajectory of 50 GW of renewable energy capacity through FY28, provides visibility to developers and investors. It also highlighted govt’s decision to allow up to 100% foreign direct investment in the electricity sector.Among the measures aimed at reducing project development risks, the analysis cited the Ultra Mega Renewable Energy Power Parks scheme, which provides developers access to land and transmission infrastructure, along with capital and interest subsidies for renewable energy projects. It also pointed to viability gap funding for offshore wind projects, including support for the development of India's first offshore wind farms.On the demand side, the report said renewable consumption obligations, which require distribution companies and large industrial and commercial consumers to source a specified proportion of their electricity from renewable sources, have helped create an expanding market for green power. Access to day-ahead and intra-day power exchanges has also widened avenues for generators to sell electricity.The analysis also highlighted measures introduced by govt in 2022 to address delays in payments by distribution companies to power generators, which had been a major concern for renewable energy developers. Outstanding dues of distribution companies, which stood at Rs 1.4 lakh crore in 2022, declined to Rs 4,109 crore in Feb 2026, it said.The report estimated that capital expenditure on solar and onshore wind projects across emerging and developing economies could reach $356 billion by 2040 if current trends continue.A senior industry executive said India’s policies to boost investment in the renewable energy sector over the past two decades had catalysed green energy growth and helped the country meet its Paris Agreement goals ahead of schedule. “Further investment focus is now required in the country’s solar supply chain. India will continue to lead in renewable energy growth and investment attractiveness, thanks to the conducive policy environment and resilience of the Indian solar industry,” the executive said.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'We will navigate through challenges': IndiGo CEO Willie Walsh on airline industry's tough phase
articles.summary: IndiGo sees significant growth opportunities despite rising fuel costs and other pressures facing the aviation industry, CEO Willie Walsh said on Monday,
articles.body: IndiGo sees significant growth opportunities despite rising fuel costs and other pressures facing the aviation industry, CEO Willie Walsh said on Monday, adding that the airline would focus on maintaining a competitive cost base while navigating the challenges.At his first in-person briefing since taking charge as chief executive in August, Walsh said IndiGo expected to begin receiving wide-body Airbus A350 aircraft from the second quarter of 2028.He said the airline had all the necessary ingredients to succeed in the long-haul market."We see incredible opportunities," Walsh said, while acknowledging the difficult operating environment for airlines.The industry is facing pressure from higher fuel costs, which have affected airline profitability. IndiGo reported a net loss of Rs 1,879.1 crore in the July-September quarter, with elevated fuel expenses and rupee depreciation weighing on its financial performance."The situation is challenging for the industry and we will continue to navigate through the challenges," Walsh said.IndiGo focuses on costs amid elevated fuel expensesThe airline has also reduced capacity in response to the operating pressures. In the September quarter, its fuel expenses rose to Rs 9,966.8 crore, an increase of 67.2% from Rs 5,961.8 crore in the corresponding period last year.IndiGo's capacity, measured in available seat kilometres, declined 1% to 40.8 billion during the quarter.Despite a 4.7% fall in passenger numbers to 2.7 crore, passenger ticket revenue increased 29.3% to Rs 20,652.2 crore, while the load factor declined 2.2 percentage points to 80.3%.Walsh had said last week that the airline expected elevated fuel costs to persist for some time and would continue exploring internal measures to offset the increase.The airline's September-quarter loss was its third consecutive quarterly loss, as per the earlier report. Its total income, however, rose 24% year-on-year to Rs 24,311.9 crore.A350 deliveries and Navi Mumbai airport plansOn IndiGo's expansion plans, Walsh said the airline expected deliveries of its wide-body A350 aircraft to begin in the second quarter of 2028. He said the carrier was well placed to enter the long-haul market.Walsh also described the upcoming Navi Mumbai airport as a significant opportunity for the airline. He said IndiGo's decision to shift some of its international flights to the new airport had been taken in the airline's interest.IndiGo currently operates more than 2,100 flights daily and has an operational fleet of over 400 aircraft.As of September 30, the airline had a fleet of 442 aircraft and operated a peak of 2,020 daily flights during the July-September quarter, including non-scheduled services.The airline's cash balance stood at Rs 52,685.4 crore at the end of September, comprising Rs 39,929 crore in free cash and Rs 12,756.4 crore in restricted cash. Its total debt, including capitalised operating lease liabilities, was Rs 87,303.1 crore, the report said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: India among world's best-performing markets in October as investors rotate away from AI stocks: Goldman Sachs
articles.summary: Indian equities were reportedly among the world's best-performing markets in October, outperforming the broader Asia-Pacific region as investors shifted
articles.body: Indian equities were reportedly among the world's best-performing markets in October, outperforming the broader Asia-Pacific region as investors shifted money away from AI-sensitive technology stocks and towards other sectors. The trend was also visible within India, where IT services stocks gained ground while companies linked to the AI ecosystem lagged, according to a Goldman Sachs Research report.The Nifty outperformed the broader Asia-Pacific region excluding Japan (MXAPJ) by 7 percentage points, reversing its underperformance during the first nine months of 2026.The change in investor preference was particularly sharp within India's technology space. Stocks classified as AI enablers, which had beaten the Nifty by 76 percentage points between January and September, underperformed the benchmark by 6 percentage points in October. IT services companies moved in the opposite direction, outperforming the index by 14 percentage points to become the month's leading sector.Goldman Sachs attributed India's gains to a broader shift in global portfolios. “India benefited from market rotation away from AI-sensitive North Asian markets,” the report said, describing the country as one of the world's best-performing markets in October, as cited by ANI.The recovery followed a difficult third quarter, when the Nifty had fallen 10 per cent from its peak to its trough. It recovered 3 per cent from its early-October low. Momentum continued in the week ended October 30, with the benchmark gaining 2 per cent against a 1 per cent rise in MXAPJ.The latest advance was not limited to large-cap stocks. Mid-cap and small-cap shares rose 3-4 per cent during the week, while pharmaceuticals gained 7 per cent. Financial stocks were relatively subdued, advancing just 1 per cent.Institutional flows also showed signs of improvement. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) bought $1.2 billion worth of Indian equities during the week, although their net outflows for 2026 remained high at $31 billion. Domestic institutional investors (DIIs) added $400 million, taking their purchases for the year to $75 billion.Earnings have provided another source of support. Companies accounting for 58 per cent of the MSCI India index's market capitalisation had reported their July-September results by the time of the report. Their combined profits were tracking 15 per cent higher than a year earlier and 13 per cent above the previous quarter.The performance, however, was uneven. Metals and mining, utilities and healthcare companies delivered more positive surprises, while cement and materials and consumer discretionary firms reported more earnings misses.The rally has also made Indian equities expensive relative to regional peers. The market's forward price-to-earnings ratio stood at 18.4 times, while its valuation premium over the broader Asia-Pacific region reached 92 per cent, close to historical highs.With several large companies due to announce results in early November, investors will be looking for earnings to justify the market's elevated valuations.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Gold price prediction today: Gold prices are likely to continue trading sideways with a downward bias, says Manav Modi, Senior Analyst, Commodity Research
articles.body: Gold price prediction today: Gold prices are likely to continue trading sideways with a downward bias, says Manav Modi, Senior Analyst, Commodity Research at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd. Let’s take a look at his detailed analysis:Gold enters week near Rs 138,500 after extending its October correction, with the hourly structure continuing to reflect a clear sequence of lower highs and lower lows. Prices have declined sharply from above Rs 151,000 earlier in October and are currently trading well below the 20-period average near Rs 140,660, confirming continued selling pressure.The Bollinger Bands are placed around Rs 143,877 on the upside and Rs 137,442 on the downside, with prices trading close to the lower band after the latest breakdown. Immediate support is placed around Rs 137,400–138,000, followed by Rs 135,000–136,000; a sustained break below this zone could expose Rs 132,000–133,000.On the upside, Rs 140,500–141,000 is now the first important hurdle, followed by Rs 143,000–144,000. A sustained recovery above Rs 144,000 would be required to meaningfully improve the short-term structure and could open the way towards Rs 146,000–147,000.Overall, the near-term technical bias remains sideways to lower below Rs 141,000, although the magnitude and speed of the recent correction increase the possibility of short-covering or a technical rebound. For the broader structure, reclaiming Rs 144,000–146,000 would be necessary before considering the correction to be stabilising.Gold enters the week attempting to recover towards $3,900 following another sharp correction, with bargain hunting and persistent geopolitical uncertainty providing support at lower levels. However, the broader macro environment remains challenging as a liquidity adjustment across global markets has triggered selling across multiple asset classes.The recent AI-led correction in technology shares has encouraged investors to reduce risk and meet margin requirements, resulting in profit-booking across gold and silver following their substantial earlier rallies. This helps explain why bullion has struggled to benefit fully from equity-market weakness and geopolitical uncertainty, as gold has temporarily been used as a source of liquidity rather than purely as a safe-haven asset.Treasury yields remain another major headwind. Long-dated US yields near 5.5% offer investors increasingly attractive risk-free returns while simultaneously tightening financial conditions beyond the Federal Reserve’s policy rate. Elevated yields increase gold’s opportunity cost and have contributed to the recent liquidation.At the same time, persistently high borrowing costs are increasing concerns over US debt-servicing expenses, fiscal sustainability and eventually economic growth. This creates a mixed environment: yields remain negative for gold in the immediate term, but the fiscal consequences of sustaining such high rates could strengthen bullion’s longer-term diversification case.Monetary policy remains restrictive after the Fed kept rates unchanged at 3.75%–4.00%, while retaining the possibility of another increase if inflation remains persistent.The absence of a clear dovish pivot keeps real yields elevated and leaves bullion sensitive to incoming inflation and labour-market data. Markets will therefore closely monitor whether softer economic activity begins to outweigh persistent inflation risks in determining the next policy move.Geopolitical risks continue to provide an underlying floor. Uncertainty surrounding US–Iran relations and the broader Middle East remains supportive of defensive demand, although gold’s response has been restrained by the stronger influence of yields and liquidity conditions.Meanwhile, dip buying from Chinese investors and longer-term strategic buyers appears to be emerging following the substantial correction, helping prices stabilise around lower levels.Attention now shifts towards the US midterm elections and upcoming labour-market data. The election outcome could materially influence expectations surrounding fiscal policy, government spending, Treasury issuance and political uncertainty, while employment data will be important in determining whether the Fed retains room for another hike.Overall, gold remains vulnerable to elevated real yields and further cross-asset liquidation in the near term, but bargain hunting, geopolitical uncertainty, Chinese demand and growing concerns surrounding US fiscal sustainability could provide an increasingly important floor following the sharp October correction.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. articles.title: Transferred Post Office employees posed as authorised staff, collected money for fake NSCs and term deposits in Rs 36.4 lakh fraud; Madhya Pradesh HC directs Post Office to process victims' claims
articles.summary: Imagine a scenario where you open some post office savings accounts, but it turns out that the accounts are fake because the people who took the deposits
articles.body: Imagine a scenario where you open some post office savings accounts, but it turns out that the accounts are fake because the people who took the deposits were not authorised to do so and scammed you!In a recent ruling by the Madhya Pradesh High Court some people at the India Post Office's Bina branch duped several depositors by issuing them counterfeit National Savings Certificates (NSCs) and term deposit advice slips. The fraud involved approximately Rs 36.4 lakh.What the case is aboutAccording to the submissions made before the court, the depositors had visited the Bina post office intending to invest in a term deposit account and a National Savings Certificate (NSC). Before they could approach the counter, however, some employees approached them, offered to assist with the paperwork and collected the money from them. These employees allegedly misrepresented their authority and subsequently handed over fabricated account statements and passbooks to the customers.The fraud came to light later, when the depositors discovered that the documents they had received were forged and that no accounts had actually been opened in their names. Despite the losses suffered by the customers, the Department of Posts declined to return their money, according to an ET report.The department argued that the depositors had dealt with an employee who had already been transferred and was no longer posted at the Bina branch when the transactions took place. According to the postal authorities, customers should have approached the authorised officials at the counter instead of relying on employees who were not assigned to that branch.The affected depositors, however, maintained that the fraud had been carried out through the actions of postal department employees. They argued that the department should therefore bear vicarious liability and compensate them for the financial losses caused by the fraudulent activities of its staff.The advocate representing the depositors argued that there was no dispute over the fact that the forged passbooks had been issued and the purported accounts opened through individuals who were employees of the Department of Posts.The depositors had no reason to doubt the identity or authority of these individuals, he contended. They could not reasonably have been expected to know whether an employee present at the post office was officially posted at that particular branch.The lawyer representing the postal department opposed the claims for compensation. The department maintained that it could not be held responsible for the money lost because the victims had not carried out their NSC and term deposit transactions through authorised staff at the counter. Instead, they had dealt with employees who were not posted at the Bina branch at the time.Madhya Pradesh Police arrested the employees responsible, who were subsequently prosecuted and convicted. Despite this, the postal department declined to compensate the affected depositors, arguing that they had failed to check whether the employees were authorised to operate at the Bina post office.The department acknowledged that the individuals involved were its employees but maintained that they had not been officially assigned to the Bina branch. However, these employees were present on the premises and allegedly targeted customers visiting the post office to open NSC and term deposit accounts.The victims eventually secured relief from the Madhya Pradesh High Court on October 15, 2026. The court directed the Department of Posts to return the money lost by the depositors, along with applicable interest.Why did the depositors succeed in their case?Nivedita Bhardwaj, Partner at King Stubb and Kasiva, told ET that the depositors won because the Madhya Pradesh High Court accepted that they had acted in good faith and conducted their transactions with individuals who were employees of the postal department. The employees had assisted them in opening accounts and issued passbooks, which were subsequently discovered to be fake. The employees were later prosecuted and convicted for their role in the fraud.The High Court pointed out that an ordinary depositor could not be expected to have knowledge of the department's internal transfer and posting arrangements, particularly when the employees concerned were present inside the post office, according to the ET report on the judgement.The Madhya Pradesh High Court said an examination of the case records showed that the depositors had been approached at the post office by individuals who were admittedly employees of the Department of Posts. The customers had no knowledge of whether these employees were assigned to the Bina branch, nor could they be expected to know about the department's internal posting arrangements.The Madhya Pradesh High Court said: “Therefore, once the petitioners (victims) acted bona fide and innocently and opened their accounts with the concerned Post Office at the behest of the said persons who were later found to be culprits, the petitioners (victims) were entitled for the amount as claimed by them after the fraud was committed.”It also referred to the department's circular dated May 27, 2021, which specifically lays down a procedure for handling situations in which an account has not actually been opened or a fraudulent passbook has been issued.On this basis, the High Court directed the postal department to entertain the claims submitted by the victims. It instructed the depositors to complete the prescribed form and submit it to the competent authority within 30 working days. Once the applications are received, the authority must examine and process the claims within 90 days.The court further held that the victims would be entitled to interest applicable to their fixed deposits, in accordance with the law.Bhardwaj said depositors should take care to route all their investments through the authorised channels of the post office. They should also collect and retain official records relating to their deposits, including passbooks, deposit receipts, account particulars and other transaction acknowledgements.Bhardwaj says: "In cases involving a fake passbook or an account that was never actually opened, depositors should also make use of the claim mechanism prescribed by the Department of Posts. The present judgment makes it clear that such situations are specifically contemplated under the Department's May 27, 2021 circular."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: China to restrict exports of giant tunnel-digging machines; why India could be affected
articles.summary: China is tightening export controls on construction equipment, including tunnel-boring machines, in a move that could affect India's infrastructure
articles.body: China is tightening export controls on construction equipment, including tunnel-boring machines, in a move that could affect India's infrastructure projects and add to concerns over its dependence on Chinese machinery.The new restrictions cover specialised equipment used to build tunnels for roads, railways and metro networks, as well as machines designed to spray concrete at high altitudes.Beijing has cited the potential military as well as civilian applications of such equipment, warning that "sensitive countries and regions with disputes with China" will face stricter export rules, Bloomberg reported.The curbs are particularly significant for India, which is among China's major customers for tunnel-boring equipment and is expanding road and railway infrastructure along the Himalayan border.The two countries have a longstanding territorial dispute in the region, where India has been building connectivity infrastructure to reduce the time required to mobilise troops.The latest restrictions are due to take effect later this month, according to Bloomberg. They also cover components, raising concerns not only about fresh procurement but also the maintenance of machinery already in use.Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings Institution, said Beijing increasingly viewed its position as a major global construction equipment producer in strategic terms."It raises the risks of dependency, and incentivizes other countries to try to de-risk from China," Chan said.Why the restrictions matter for IndiaChina accounts for around 70% of the global tunnel-boring machine market, according to Chinese state media figures cited by Bloomberg. Its leading manufacturer, China Railway Engineering Equipment Group Co Ltd, says its machinery is used in 36 countries, including Denmark and France.India has previously faced delays in procuring Chinese-made tunnelling equipment.In 2024, China delayed efforts by German manufacturer Herrenknecht AG to sell tunnel-boring machines to India for projects including the Ahmedabad-Mumbai bullet train and the Delhi Metro.A spokesperson for Herrenknecht said the company was studying the latest Chinese restrictions.The new controls could also affect the supply of spare parts. Ajay Srivastava, founder of the New Delhi-based Global Trade Research Initiative, said India could shift equipment between priority projects if necessary, but restrictions on components could create difficulties for existing machinery."When there is heavy wear and tear in these machines we require regular supply of parts," Srivastava said, adding that the curbs could affect both the existing stock of machines and the procurement of new ones.The inclusion of equipment used for concrete spraying at high altitudes has also drawn attention. Sun Chenghao, a fellow at Tsinghua University's Center for International Security and Strategy in Beijing, said this could indicate a particular focus on "strategically sensitive terrain"."For China, the central concern is where Chinese engineering capabilities are used and whether they could strengthen another country's military infrastructure," Sun said.India looks to reduce dependence on Chinese machineryThe restrictions come as India seeks to expand domestic manufacturing of high-value construction and infrastructure equipment.The government is considering a $1.2-billion incentive scheme for manufacturers of equipment such as tunnel-boring machines, firefighting systems and elevators.The proposed programme is expected to attract around $1.8 billion in fresh investment by offering incentives to domestic manufacturers over seven years. It is also expected to include local value-addition targets for machinery that is currently imported.The scheme was announced in the 2026-27 Union Budget as part of efforts to strengthen domestic production of technologically advanced construction and infrastructure equipment. State-run BEML, along with private-sector companies such as Larsen & Toubro and Johnson Lifts, could benefit from the proposed incentives, according to the earlier report.India's infrastructure expansion is expected to drive demand for specialised equipment. Road transport and highways minister Nitin Gadkari has said the country aims to invest up to $9.6 billion in tunnelling over the next five years and has urged domestic industry to manufacture tunnel-boring machines.Domestic manufacturing faces cost challengesLarsen & Toubro, one of India's major engineering companies, is working on developing its own tunnel-boring machine.R Shankar Raman, president of the Mumbai-based company, said L&T was building a prototype and could eventually manufacture machinery for its own projects and other buyers if the experiment proved successful.However, he cautioned that India's manufacturing industry was still at an earlier stage, while Chinese manufacturers benefited from large-scale production."If people are still going to compare with Chinese price and find ways to import from China," Raman said, "then India will be at a disadvantage."Bloomberg Economics said the restrictions could slow some infrastructure projects, including strategic construction along the disputed Himalayan border.However, it also noted that tighter Chinese export controls could strengthen India's case as an alternative manufacturing base, encouraging foreign equipment makers to add capacity in the country.Besides Herrenknecht, manufacturers in the US and Japan also produce potential alternatives to Chinese tunnelling equipment. However, switching suppliers in the short term could be difficult for customers that rely heavily on Chinese machinery.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: India's manufacturing PMI eases to 54.7 in October as export orders hit six-month high
articles.summary: India's manufacturing activity expanded at a slower pace in October as growth in output and new orders moderated, although stronger overseas demand
articles.body: India's manufacturing activity expanded at a slower pace in October as growth in output and new orders moderated, although stronger overseas demand supported production and helped cushion the slowdown.Factory employment continued to rise, while input cost inflation eased to its lowest level since February, a monthly survey showed on Monday.The seasonally adjusted HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI), compiled by S&P Global, fell to 54.7 in October from 55.1 in September.Despite the decline, the index remained above its long-run average and comfortably higher than the neutral mark of 50, which separates expansion from contraction.Growth in new business remained strong, although it eased marginally from September's seven-month high. New export orders, however, increased at their fastest pace in six months, according to the survey.Manufacturers reported higher demand from markets including Bangladesh, Canada, Indonesia, Nepal, Oman, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, the UK, the US and the UAE."Strong international demand pushed growth of new export orders to a six-month high, supporting a robust rise in output," said Pranjul Bhandari, chief India economist at HSBC.Output rises, but hiring growth remains subduedStronger overseas demand supported an increase in factory output, although the pace of production growth softened from September. The survey attributed the rise in new business to favourable demand trends, new client wins and successful marketing campaigns.Manufacturers continued to build inventories during the month. Input inventories increased at the fastest pace in eight months as companies built precautionary buffers against potential shortages and prepared to meet production requirements in a volatile global environment.Firms also increased their stocks of finished goods at a record pace in the survey's more than 21-year history, according to Reuters. Manufacturers cited buoyant demand and efforts to prevent shortages.However, the pace of raw material purchasing growth slowed to its weakest in the 64-month sequence of expansion.Factory employment increased for the second consecutive month as higher production requirements and rising workloads encouraged companies to recruit more workers. However, the pace of job creation eased from September.Capital goods manufacturers reduced staff during the month.Input cost inflation falls to lowest since FebruaryCost pressures moderated across all three broad areas of India's manufacturing industry monitored by the survey. Although manufacturers reported higher prices for some materials and energy, the overall rate of input cost inflation declined to its lowest level since February.Selling price inflation also weakened. The increase in output prices was the slowest in nearly four years."Although some material and energy costs increased, overall input and output price pressures eased slightly from the previous month," Bhandari said.Business confidence weakensDespite continued growth in demand, manufacturers became less optimistic about the year ahead. Business confidence slipped from September and remained below its long-run average, the survey said.Close to 18 per cent of manufacturers expected output to increase over the coming year, while the rest were neutral. Expectations of higher production were supported by new client enquiries and demand for industrial automation and technology solutions.The HSBC India Manufacturing PMI is compiled by S&P Global from responses to questionnaires sent to purchasing managers at a panel of around 400 manufacturers.You use AI every day. articles.title: LTCG tax relief on the cards? SEBI wants long-term capital gains tax to be removed for foreign investors
articles.summary: The buzz around removal of long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax on equities is gaining traction, with the market regulator also urging the government to
articles.body: The buzz around removal of long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax on equities is gaining traction, with the market regulator also urging the government to scrap it. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has reportedly requested the government to consider scrapping LTCG tax levied on foreign investors.The proposal comes as authorities look for ways to revive India's equity markets, which have been performing below the level of their emerging market counterparts.According to a Reuters report, SEBI has also suggested extending tax relief to domestic mutual fund investors. Under its proposal, investors switching from existing mutual fund holdings to other schemes would not have to pay LTCG tax on the transaction, sources quoted in the report said.The recommendations have been submitted ahead of the annual Union Budget scheduled for February. However, they are advisory in nature, and the final decision on whether to accept them rests with the government.Stock market turmoilIndian equities have underperformed other emerging markets over the past two years. Foreign investors have withdrawn a record $31 billion from Indian stocks so far this year, while retail investors have increased their overseas investments as domestic market returns have remained subdued.SEBI's proposals follow numerous discussions the regulator has held with foreign investors over the past two years, even as continued selling by overseas funds has put pressure on the Indian currency.A recurring concern raised during these interactions has been India's tax treatment of foreign investors, the sources said."The proposals are aimed at reducing the upfront tax burden on foreign investors," one of the two sources told Reuters.SEBI has pointed out that the costs of investing in Indian equities are among the highest when compared with other markets.At present, investors are required to pay LTCG tax of 12.5% on securities held for more than a year. Short-term capital gains are taxed at 20%. These levies are in addition to securities transaction taxes on trades and withholding taxes on dividend income.In a note issued earlier this week, brokerage firm Jefferies said lowering capital gains taxes could make Indian equities more appealing to overseas investors and help attract portfolio inflows.Brokerage IIFL has estimated that doing away with capital gains tax could increase foreign investors' returns by 2.3 percentage points.The underperformance of Indian equities has also affected domestic investors. The benchmark Nifty 50 has fallen 4.8% over the past two years, whereas the MSCI emerging markets index has gained 40%.Returns from diversified domestic equity mutual funds, which have become a popular investment avenue among retail savers, have remained weak during the same period. Data from fund research firm Morningstar shows that large-cap mutual funds have delivered average returns of minus 1.6%.SEBI wants to encourage investors to continue investing in domestic mutual funds. To achieve this, it has been proposed that moving investments from one mutual fund scheme to another should not trigger a tax liability, provided the original units have been held for more than a year, the sources said.The domestic mutual fund industry currently manages assets worth Rs 82.6 trillion ($870.80 billion). Monthly investment schemes bring in an average of Rs 30 billion every month.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: At 1,000 this fiscal, IndiGo set to hire most pilots in a year by an Indian carrier
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: In the largest ever cockpit crew hiring by an Indian airline, IndiGo has on boarded 600 pilots in the first six months of this fiscal and is on
articles.body: NEW DELHI: In the largest ever cockpit crew hiring by an Indian airline, IndiGo has on boarded 600 pilots in the first six months of this fiscal and is on track to add at least 400 more by next March-end, say people in the know. The airline had committed to add pilots after witnessing an unprecedented schedule collapse last Dec. IndiGo had 5,700 pilots as on March 31, 2026, and this number rose to 6,300 by Sept end.The flight duty time limitation (FDTL, which regulate pilot duty norms) dispensation will end next March and IndiGo’s CEO Willie Walsh said on Monday in his first interaction with the media in this role that the airline will have “more than enough pilots to meet the schedules that we have for the airline. We're confident that of fully complying with the FDTL regulations.”A trained pilot, Willie — who headed British Airways and International Air Transport Association before joining IndiGo this Aug — will spearhead the budget airline’s international expansion over coming years amid the unprecedented challenges being faced by aviation globally. IndiGo, which used to be India’s only profitable airline, has also flown into losses for the past few quarters.“The geopolitical situation is challenging. Aviation turbine fuel accounts for 32% of airlines’ operating cost globally. In India, that figure is higher at 40%. The concerning thing is the crack spread (price difference between a barrel of crude oil and the petroleum products like ATF refined from it). Crude prices have not gone that high but the premium on ATF pricing has risen. Luckily availability of ATF is not an issue in India which exports jet fuel,” said Walsh.Airlines have not fully passed on the hike in operating cost and have taken other measures like cutting capacity in the lean travel July-Sept quarter. Also due to geopolitical reasons flights have been cut. Saudi flights are impacted right now, with IndiGo also cutting the same.“No Indian carrier does fuel hedging. We are weighing that option for long hauls expansion. We expect to get our Airbus A350s from the second quarter of 2028. As of now we have four A321 XLRs (extra long range) and will get more of these planes next year,” said Walsh. IndiGo has 60 A350s on firm order. “We will have a business class with 16 flat bed seats, premium economy and economy sections in the first 10 A350s. Then we will see whether to increase the number of business class seats in subsequent deliveries. I personally think there will be a case of doing so,” said Walsh.The closure of Pakistan airspace for Indian carriers has impacted western routes to and from Delhi. Air India and IndiGo now add flights to the west mainly from Mumbai. “The Navi Mumbai airport is a business opportunity for IndiGo as our long haul international expansion in the future will be also from Mumbai and Navi Mumbai (apart from other places like Delhi and Bengaluru).”Walsh, however, cautioned overall airport charges in India are “too high.” “Indian aviation market will do much better with lower charges and taxes,” he said.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'More and more disenchanted': A final check-in on Trump's economic approval ratings before midterms
articles.summary: President Trump's economic approval ratings are hovering at second-term lows.
articles.body:
President Trump's economic approval ratings are hovering at second-term lows, with inflation worries the central headwind for the president and his party as the midterm elections loom.

A raft of recent polls underscores this reality: Trump's low overall approval ratings are being dragged down by economic sentiment that is even lower.

A new national poll released on Sunday by NBC News found that a majority of Republicans — 53% — say they are dissatisfied with the state of the economy.

And inflation remains the top-of-mind issue, with only about 25.3% of voters approving of Trump's handling of inflation versus 69.5% who disapprove, according to an average of recent polls calculated on Sunday by forecaster Nate Silver.

Another tabulation from RealClearPolitics this past weekend showed a 70.4% disapproval rating of the president's handling of prices, which voters often say is their top issue.

Deep voter dissatisfaction is evident on other financial issues like tariffs and taxes. The president is facing a negative net rating of -29.7% on trade and -31.1% on the economy overall, according to Silver, with this economic drag outpacing Trump's overall net approval rating of -22.6%.

As Ipsos summarized their results this past week, "American consumers have grown more and more disenchanted with the economy and the Trump administration," noting that disapproval of Trump's handling of the economy has nearly doubled since his inauguration and remains the No. 1 issue for voters .

"All that spells trouble for Republicans across the nation on Tuesday," the pollsters concluded.

Economic dissatisfaction with both Trump and his party

Democrats, meanwhile, are hitting new highs ahead of the election even as voters often give the opposition party mixed marks overall .

Those results are being fueled by respondents who listed inflation as their top issue. In a Focaldata-Financial Times poll this past week, 47% of respondents said Democrats would do a better job handling that issue versus 34% who said the same about Republicans.

One possible glimmer of hope for Republicans in that data: 20% of voters say they are either unsure or that neither party would do a better job.

The data for the GOP has become so challenging that some results show voters are inclined to dismiss Republicans' record on taxes, an issue that historically has been a strength and a centerpiece of Trump's economic agenda over the last two years.

"I signed the Great Big Beautiful Bill, delivering the largest tax cuts in American history, including no tax on tips, no tax on overtime, no tax on Social Security," the president said Thursday in South Carolina .

articles.title: Here’s where Trump’s housing agenda stands before midterms
articles.summary: America’s housing market is paralyzed, with buyers pulling back and builders growing more pessimistic ahead of the midterms.
articles.body: America’s housing market is paralyzed, with buyers pulling back and builders growing more pessimistic ahead of the midterms. Adding to the strain: Mortgage rates have surged back above 7% in recent weeks, hitting a three-year high of 7.4% last month. The average 30-year fixed rate eased slightly to 7.24% last week, according to Freddie Mac. America’s housing woes run deep. Homebuilding hasn’t kept pace with demand since the 2008 financial crash decimated the country’s housing industry. Elevated mortgage rates have also pushed up monthly payments for buyers, all while home prices keep climbing each month to record-high levels. As of the third quarter, the average household must earn $115,600 in income to afford the typical cost of housing – that’s 75% higher than the $66,200 required five years ago, according to Oxford Economics. That has translated to the number of homes trading hands to hover near 30-year lows for the past three years. President Donald Trump won the 2024 election amid growing frustration over the cost of living. Two years later, affordability remains a defining issue heading into the midterm elections, as Americans continue to grapple with high prices for housing, groceries, gasoline and other everyday essentials. But while the White House has taken some steps aimed at housing affordability during Trump’s second term, largely through executive orders, the issue has featured relatively little in the administration’s public messaging over the last two years. Trump, who was a real estate developer for decades, said on the 2024 campaign trail that his plan for tackling the cost of housing would primarily rely on lowering interest rates. He doubled down on that promise this year. “People that own their homes, we’re going to keep them wealthy. We’re going to keep those prices up. We’re not going to destroy the value of their homes,” Trump said at a cabinet meeting at the start of this year. “We’re going to make it easier to buy. We’re going to get interest rates down.” For a brief moment, mortgage rates appeared poised to fall. In January, Trump directed Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, the government-sponsored enterprises that underpin much of the US mortgage market, to buy $200 billion in mortgage-backed securities in an effort to push rates lower. Rates dropped earlier in the year, dipping below 6% in February for the first time since 2022, when the Federal Reserve began its fight against post-pandemic inflation, raising hopes that cheaper borrowing would ease the housing affordability crunch. But the reprieve was short-lived. Mortgage rates climbed once again after the US began its war with Iran, and have remained elevated since. Mortgage rates are tied to the 10-year Treasury yield, which moves with investors’ expectations for inflation, economic growth and the Fed’s interest rate policy. In recent months, the bond market has been hit by renewed inflation fears, an oil-price shock linked to the Iran conflict, rising federal deficits and a surge in AI investment. And early signs point to the bond market turmoil adding to the housing market’s woes. Pending home sales fell to a record low in September, in data going back to 2001, according to the National Association of Realtors. New home construction also dropped to a four-month low, Census Bureau data showed, as elevated borrowing costs continue to weigh on the market. The gloom is spreading to builders, too: Homebuilder sentiment, a measure of how confident the industry feels about the housing market, sank to a 14-year low in September, according to the latest survey from the National Association of Home Builders. Overall, the housing market’s issues are going to take a long time to solve. But some bright spots remain: Rents have stabilized nationally over the last few years, said Yonah Freemark, a principal research associate in the Housing and Communities Division at the Urban Institute. That’s partly due to increased multifamily apartment construction between 2020 and 2024, which helped relieve demand pressures, he added. Trump’s complicated housing agenda Overall, the federal government may not have much power to affect the housing market’s supply, because zoning and permitting decisions are made by local and state governments, said Daryl Fairweather, Redfin’s chief economist. “In places that have been builder-friendly and have allowed supply to meet demand, we have seen prices come down and affordability improve,” Fairweather said, pointing to Austin, Texas, as an example, which has seen home prices fall from their peak in 2022. The city expanded its housing stock by roughly 30% between 2015 and 2024, according to Pew. Last month, Trump signed an executive order that directs federal agencies to ease the burden of mortgage insurance and refinance costs, among other measures. “President Trump has been laser-focused on making housing more affordable,” said Davis Ingle, a White House spokesperson. “The President will not stop fighting until the American Dream of homeownership is within reach for every American, which is why he continues to sign bold new executive orders and calls on Congress to pass further legislation.” But the White House’s tariff regime has added to the cost of building housing, according to the NAHB – and deportations have slowed home-building projects in many areas that rely on an immigrant construction workforce. Some White House proposals to improve housing affordability never materialized, such as a 50-year mortgage or the ability to make mortgages portable, which would allow homeowners with lower rates to take their existing loan to a new property when they move. Most housing initiatives were also handled by executive order, rather than through legislation. The one exception was the ROAD to Housing Act, which Congress passed with broad bipartisan support this summer. The bill included measures to increase the supply of housing and a provision to limit large investor purchases of single-family homes, which codified into law one of Trump’s executive orders. articles.title: EJ ANTONI: Overseas wars put affordability on hold, but that’s only temporary
articles.summary: Real paychecks lost 4% in purchasing power under Biden, and overseas energy shocks are now reversing the affordability gains made in early 2025.
articles.body: American families aren’t imagining it: we’ve had affordability problems since at least 2022. The situation was improving markedly throughout last year, right up until this February, but overseas conflicts reversed some of that progress. Once the wars with Iran and in Ukraine conclude, affordability will start to improve again. The cost-of-living crisis started during the Biden administration when prices rose so much faster than earnings that people’s paychecks shrunk in terms of their purchasing power. Although the average American’s weekly paycheck grew roughly 17% during President Joe Biden’s term, it bought about 4% less. For many families, that meant canceling vacation plans or being unable to buy a newer vehicle. For others, it meant having to put some necessities — like rent, prescriptions and food — on credit cards. Even when inflation came down, families were still facing high costs since inflation is the rate of price increases, not the prices themselves. DEMOCRATS SAY THEY'LL MAKE LIFE AFFORDABLE. YOUR WALLET MAY DISAGREE To add insult to injury, 40-year-high inflation prompted the fastest rise in interest rates in just as long. Not only did prices rise rapidly, but so did borrowing costs. That was a deadly one-two punch for homeownership affordability as higher home prices and mortgage interest rates combined to double the monthly payment on a median-priced home in just four years. But affordability was improving after January 2025. Real (inflation-adjusted) weekly paychecks rose roughly 2% on average from January 2025 through February of this year. While not a windfall, it was still good progress and reversed half the cumulative losses from the Biden years as income growth outpaced inflation. GEN Z IS WORKING HARD, BUT THE ECONOMY IS PUTTING THE AMERICAN DREAM OUT OF REACH FOR MANY Tax and regulatory reform, along with sound energy policy, were spurring economic activity and wage growth while keeping inflation down. Then the Iran war broke out. Global energy markets specifically and supply chains broadly were severely disrupted, causing costs to skyrocket. Oil prices quickly rose from $60 or $70 per barrel, depending on the market, to $100 or $120. Prices at the pump soon followed, but the energy shock is spilling over to more sectors of the economy with each passing day. CHEVRON CEO WARNS IRAN CONFLICT HAS CREATED 'VERY REAL' THREAT TO GLOBAL OIL SUPPLIES AS GAS PRICES CLIMB Energy is an input cost in every product and service consumers buy. Food at the grocery store was grown with diesel-powered tractors and fertilizer synthesized from natural gas. It was transported to the store on a truck, and maybe a train too, fueled by diesel. Prices for everything from airfares to plastics to manufactured goods are up because of the energy shock. The reversal in progress on affordability is evident in housing too. Homeownership affordability hit a three-year high in February and, while still relatively low, marked a significant improvement from the record low in the Biden years. However, it’s fallen each month since then to the lowest level since July 2024 as interest rates ramped up. THE OVERLOOKED WAY THE IRAN WAR IS MAKING GROCERIES, AMAZON PACKAGES AND NEW HOMES MORE EXPENSIVE Those higher mortgage interest rates are also a result of the current energy shock. When fuel supplies began falling, energy prices rose, and that in turn drove inflation expectations higher. Interest rates followed as lenders demanded a higher return for the anticipated inflation. And the disruptions are not just from the Middle East, but Eastern Europe too. Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure have exacerbated the shortage of oil and petroleum products, especially diesel. The result was higher prices and lower real earnings. AMERICA'S TRUCKERS ISSUE DIRE WARNING AS SOARING DIESEL COSTS THREATEN 'DOMINO EFFECT' However, unlike the runaway inflation that peaked in 2022 at an annual rate exceeding 9%, today’s higher prices are not from the government devaluing the currency by spending, borrowing and creating too much money. Rather, this is an energy shock that is causing countless prices to rise. The difference in causation means there’s a different solution and a better outlook too. The affordability crisis was easing significantly until the energy shocks hit, and those shocks came from overseas. There’s nothing wrong with the domestic fundamentals underpinning the American economy. LEE ZELDIN: BIDEN'S ENERGY RULES COST BILLIONS. TRUMP'S EPA IS LOWERING COSTS Investment is booming. The manufacturing sector is expanding at the fastest pace in at least four years. The private sector is adding jobs. AI is fueling productivity growth and earnings are still growing. Once the conflicts overseas are resolved, energy markets will begin to normalize and costs will start declining. Then the economy will be firing on all cylinders. Likewise, inflation expectations will fall, dragging interest rates back down and improving homeownership affordability. Falling prices and rising earnings mean more breathing room for families. articles.title: 5 charts that explain the economy’s role in the midterm elections
articles.summary: On Election Day, Americans will answer the question of whether they’re better off than they were two years ago when they cast ballots in the midterms.
articles.body: Back in 1980, Ronald Reagan asked, “Are you better off than you were four years ago?” On Tuesday, millions of Americans will answer for themselves whether they are better off than they were two years ago, when they vote in the midterm elections. Top of mind for many Americans: the economy. In a recent NBC News Decision Desk Poll, the economy ranked as the issue that matters most to voters and one on which a majority say they are deeply frustrated with President Donald Trump. Here are the five charts that explain why. The cost of living At the start of Trump’s second term, paychecks were rising faster than prices. But consumer prices have soared since the war with Iran started, and for the last six months, inflation has outpaced wage gains. In September, inflation jumped to 3.7%, while wages rose just 3% from a year ago, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Gas prices A big driver of those rising consumer prices: spiking energy costs as a result of the war with Iran. Regular gas prices averaged $3.12 per gallon when Trump started his second term and $2.98 right before the war, according to AAA. Now they’re well above $4 — the highest regular gas prices have been just before an election. Diesel prices have surged to all-time highs in recent weeks. They were averaging $3.63 at the start of Trump’s second term and $3.75 when the war with Iran began. Now they’re well above $6. And higher costs for diesel — which powers trucks, trains and tractors — typically spill into the rest of the economy. Mortgage rates Mortgage rates topped 7% in January 2025, but they fell over the first year of Trump’s second term. The 30-year fixed rate dipped below 6% just before the Iran war, according to Freddie Mac. Since then, mortgage rates have soared — with the 30-year fixed rate well above 7% now. The 15-year fixed rate has spiked, too, jumping above 6%. Home prices Historically speaking, it’s not uncommon to see U.S. mortgage rates above 7%. But paired with average home prices that have jumped 57% since January 2020, the higher rates mean many Americans looking to buy homes are simply getting priced out of the housing market. The average price of a single-family home was $422,700 in September, according to the National Association of Realtors. At the same time that buyers are feeling priced out, homeowners are sitting on more than $35 trillion in real estate equity as of the second quarter of 2026, according to the Federal Reserve. That figure has more than doubled over the last decade. Of course, for most people it’s still money on paper — you can’t easily use it to buy a Halloween costume or fill up your gas tank. Stock market gains The stock market overall has done very well during Trump’s second term, and the S&P 500 index has soared by more than 26%. There have been a few dips, notably when Trump announced his “Liberation Day” tariffs in 2025 and then again during the early weeks of the Iran war. But artificial intelligence spending and generally strong corporate earnings have propelled the S&P 500 to record highs in recent weeks. But all that wealth in stock market gains reflects a broader divide in America: Wall Street investors’ wealth has grown over the second Trump administration. Homeowners, too, have seen their property values climb. But for millions of Americans, it’s still hard to keep up month to month, let alone get ahead — something that will be on many voters’ minds Tuesday at the ballot box.

articles.title: Reliance Adds Record $19 Billion in Market Value on Profit Beat
articles.summary: Reliance Industries Ltd. shares surged almost 12%, adding more than $19 billion in market value in a record single-day gain for an Indian company, after quar...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Reliance Industries Ltd. shares surged almost 12%, adding more than $19 billion in market value in a record single-day gain for an Indian company, after quarterly profit surpassed expectations.

The rally, the steepest since April 2020, came alongside another milestone for the oil-to-telecom giant: for the first time in nearly a decade, no analyst recommends selling the stock.

Avendus Spark, the only brokerage with a sell-equivalent rating on India's most valuable company, raised the stock to add from reduce following the conglomerate's blowout earnings. The move by analyst Arun Prasath leaves the billionaire Mukesh Ambani-led company with 32 buy calls and no hold or sell recommendations — a first since 2017, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Prasath's upgrade comes after he maintained a sell-equivalent rating for most of the past four years.

The bullish turn marks a sharp reversal in sentiment toward the index heavyweight after months of concern over earnings momentum across its businesses, including retail. The stock had fallen more than 20% this year before Monday, pushing its valuation toward multi-year lows. Avendus said the slide implied a holding-company discount of about 80% on Reliance's stake in the newly listed Jio Platforms Ltd., a level it expects to narrow.

"Such a high holding company discount is unreasonable for a mega-cap and should converge toward 25%-30% over time," Prasath, among the top-rated analysts for Reliance, wrote in a note dated Nov. 2. He has a 12-month target of 1,280 rupees.

The stock jumped almost 12% to 1,300 rupees at the close, after Friday's earnings beat revived optimism over the company's growth.

Net income surged more than 40% to 255.5 billion rupees ($2.7 billion) in the September quarter, beating the 213.67 billion-rupee average of analyst estimates compiled by Bloomberg. The results were helped by diesel refining margins near historic highs amid tight global supplies and disruptions from the Middle East war.

Jio Platforms, in which Reliance owns 64.5%, also posted a 14% rise in profit. The company's listing last week — the largest-ever for an Indian company — helped propel billionaire Ambani's Reliance Group past the Tata Group to become India's most valuable business empire.
