articles.title: Coffee’s new status symbol is a machine without plastic
articles.summary: Growing concern over ingesting microplastic is sparking a wave of plastic-free coffee pods and machines.
articles.body: For decades, it was all the bells and whistles that was the selling point for a fancy coffee machine. Now, consumers are looking for what it lacks. Growing concern over microplastics and sustainability is sparking a wave of plastic-free coffee pods and machines. Coffee companies and appliance makers have released new machines and redesigned capsules in recent months. Keurig and Lavazza’s new pods ditch the traditional plastic cups for compostable coffee tablets. Caraway’s new machine uses traditional coffee grounds, but unlike a conventional drip machine, the stainless steel and glass machine doesn’t have plastic in its brew path. More research is needed to determine the actual harm microplastics cause. But nine in 10 Americans are concerned about the effect of the minuscule plastic pieces on the planet and their bodies, according to a 2025 poll conducted by environmental group 5 Gyres; and studies have shown that pods shed microplastics. The growth in pricey equipment and plastic-free pods fits a broader pattern of consumers trading up on home coffee equipment since the pandemic, said Peter Giuliano, senior adviser for research at Specialty Coffee Association. The appeal and growth combine three things: health worries about microplastics, concern about plastic in the environment and the “feeling that metal and glass are more ‘luxury’ than plastic,” he told CNN. New pods In June, Lavazza introduced Tablì in the US, a $129 machine that uses only single-serve espresso tablets made with compressed ground coffee — a shift from its capsules made from plastic and aluminum. The tablets are made by a custom technology that “compresses precisely dosed, ground, and tamped coffee into a solid, ready-to-use tab,” Lavazza said in a press release. The Italian company says the new machine is its “largest investment yet” in the United States as it looks to double revenue to $1 billion by 2029, unlocking the stranglehold Keurig Dr. Pepper has on the coffee market. Tablì is aimed at customers who want a sustainable alternative to the traditional pod, according to Daniele Foti, vice president of marketing for Lavazza North America. “Consumers want to enjoy their coffee without the waste that usually comes with single-serve,” he told CNN. Keurig, which ushered in the boom of plastics with their K-Cups back in the 1990s, launched in October a new line of compostable pods with a specially designed machine called the Alta. (The new pods don’t fit in the old machines.) Called AltaRounds, the pods have been in development since 2020 in response to consumers’ shifting sustainability and health preferences. The new pods represent a “significant reduction in plastic compared to our K-Cup pods,” said Phil Drapeau, senior vice president for Keurig’s Future Coffee Systems unit. “We’ve heard clearly from customers that they want more sustainable products and specifically less plastic and plastic waste,” Drapeau told CNN. “Our data shows that drink variety, quality, and less plastic waste are high priorities across almost every group.” Keurig has come under fire in the past over its pods, agreeing in 2022 to pay $10 million to settle a class-action lawsuit alleging it misled consumers by marketing its plastic K-Cups as recyclable, though it denied any wrongdoing. But while the pods and the machine contain less plastic, they are considerably more expensive than a traditional Keurig machine. The Alta bundle that includes glassware and pods costs $499. Melissa Valliant, director of communications for 5 Gyres, said that both the Lavazza and Keurig products still use plastic packaging, which “ends up in a landfill, incinerator, or our environment after use, contributing to the planet’s growing plastic pollution crisis.” New machine Caraway has focused on developing a $495 coffee machine, released last month, that’s created entirely of stainless steel and glass, ensuring that no plastic touches the ground coffee. (Lavazza’s and Keurig’s machines contain some amounts of plastic.) Developing a coffee machine with plastic-free brew path was challenging, according to Caraway CEO Jordan Nathan. That’s because the pricey glass and steel parts all need to be custom-made. “We had to make the best coffee possible with no plastic on the interior with a full metal body, but also in a small (counter) footprint that had a single dial,” he told CNN. Concern over plastic in the kitchen and its affects on the endocrine system has been growing for the past few years, Nathan said, referencing a viral article that linked black plastics in the kitchen to alarming levels of toxic flame retardants. Social media, influencers and various scientific studies have all fueled the conversation, with parents and other health-conscious shoppers avoiding plastic where they can, including in makeup, food and bedding. Caraway’s other plastic-free products, like cutting boards, have soared in sales over the past three years. Coffee is a natural next step, Nathan added, because “you never want to heat plastic.” Demand for Caraway’s new 10-cup coffee maker has been so strong that it’s sold out until January, forcing the company to ramp up production. Meanwhile, Keurig and Lavazza reported similar interest with both company’s product selling out quickly after their initial release. That appetite for these pods and machines signals the industry will move toward more plastic-free alternatives, Nathan said. “If you’re not doing it, you’re behind where the puck is moving,” he concluded.

articles.title: This is the biggest threat to the AI-powered bull market
articles.summary: Blockbuster earnings growth has helped to power the stock market higher in 2026. In 2027, that engine might stall.
articles.body:
Blockbuster earnings growth has helped to power the stock market higher in 2026. In 2027, that engine might stall.

Earnings for the S&P 500 SPX are on track to grow by more than 30% this year, a pace rarely seen outside of the early innings of an economic recovery, according to Capital Economics. Profit growth is expected to moderate slightly next year and slow to 16.3%, although that is still roughly double the long-term average.

But worries that even this slower pace of growth might not materialize has helped to weigh on major indexes like the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite COMP recently. The Nasdaq finished Friday's session on the cusp of correction territory — defined as a drop of 10% or more from a recent high.

During the early years of the bull market, gains for the top-performing stocks far outpaced the earnings that analysts expected these companies to bring in over the next year. But since the start of 2026, that dynamic has been flipped on its head, as investors have become increasingly unwilling to pay up for the lofty earnings growth that Wall Street analysts are expecting.

The forward price-to-earnings ratio for the S&P 500 has been falling all year and was recently at around 19, about 20% below its peak. For the fast-growing technology sector, multiples have come down even more quickly. Some of tech's heavy hitters — like chip maker Nvidia NVDA — are trading at multiples in the midteens, roughly half of the highest levels seen in 2025.

Some have said that this is a solid indication that the stock market isn't in a bubble, since lofty valuations are usually a signpost of a market bubble forming. Others, including Damped Spring Advisors founder Andy Constan, have warned that a bubble isn't forming in stock prices but rather in projected earnings.

To Eddie Ghabour, co-founder of Key Advisors Group, investors have good reason to be skeptical about all of this expected growth. Investment-grade corporate borrowers like Amazon.com AMZN rushed to issue debt at the same time as lower-quality borrowers like CoreWeave CRWV, prompting investors to start to demand a higher premium for holding corporate debt.

articles.title: Ryanair eyes cost cuts as it faces a €2 billion rise in its fuel bill next year
articles.summary: One of Europe's biggest airlines saw its first-half profit fall 15% as higher fuel costs and lower fares outweighed passenger growth.View on euronews
articles.body:
Ryanair ( RYAAY ) reported a net profit of €2.15 billion ($2.45 billion) for the period between April and September 2026, the first half of its financial year ending March 2027.

The result was 15% below the same period last year.

This came as unhedged jet fuel prices doubled while fares also fell, although passenger numbers increased. The airline is reviewing costs as it prepares for a further rise in its fuel bill next year.

Ryanair stock rose almost 3% before the bell on Monday.

On a per-share basis, the Irish airline's first-half diluted earnings fell 14% to €2.05 per share. In the same period, revenue rose 3% to €10.08bn and passenger numbers grew by 6% to 125.8 million, but fares fell by 4%.

Ryanair said the Middle East conflict had made consumers more hesitant and led them to book later as operating costs increased by 10% to €7.69 billion.

The results reflect only part of the rise in fuel prices as Ryanair has hedged 80% of its fuel needs for the year ending March 2027, using financial contracts to lock in prices in advance.

This has helped protect its earnings, but the price of the remaining 20% doubled.

According to Ryanair, its fuel bill could rise by around €2 billion in the financial year ending March 2028, based on current forward prices.

"Unless there is a swift resolution of the Middle East conflict, we expect jet-fuel prices to remain elevated well into 2027," CEO Michael O'Leary said.

O'Leary warned that cheaper fuel hedges would expire ahead of summer 2027, leaving European airlines facing much higher bills.

He also previously warned that European airfares could rise by up to 20% in 2027 in an exclusive interview with Euronews in late October.

However, Ryanair expects higher fares and cuts in competitors' capacity to fall short of fully covering its extra fuel costs.

To address the elevated costs, Ryanair is reviewing possible cost-cutting measures, including temporary pay freezes, lower crew-to-passenger ratios and greater use of AI across operations and support teams.

The airline also announced an €800 million share buyback programme, starting in February 2027 and expected to run for around 10 months, subject to market conditions.

Demand for October–December remains strong, with fares running modestly above last year, but late bookings make the outlook harder to predict.

Ryanair said it was too early to give a full-year profit forecast, citing uncertainty over conflicts, fuel prices, the wider economy and European air traffic control disruptions.

In September, Ryanair announced it would reduce its winter schedule to limit exposure to unhedged fuel costs, cutting its full-year passenger target from 216 million to 214 million.

Ryanair's share price was up by 2% in Dublin in early trading on Monday.

articles.title: Why investors are dumping tech stocks, in one image
articles.summary: Tech stocks aren't getting shredded for any old reason. It's actually very fundamental: Free cash flow is drying up for Big Tech leaders, and capex is rising...
articles.body:
Tech stocks aren't getting shredded for any old reason. It's actually very fundamental: Free cash flow is drying up for Big Tech leaders, and capex is rising dramatically.

Investors are questioning whether this ratio is totally out of whack, given more realistic growth projections for AI.

The combined capex of Amazon, Alphabet, Meta and Microsoft rose by $36.9 billion in the third quarter to $201.9 billion, the team at The Kobeissi Letter calculated (chart below). This figure has more than doubled over the past 12 months, and is up a staggering 356% since the first quarter of 2024.

Big Tech has now spent $1.6 trillion on capex over the last three years, the strategists say. At the same time, the combined free cash flow of these companies fell $33.1 billion last quarter to a negative $26.4 billion, its lowest on record. Free cash flow among these tech beasts has fallen by $88.2 billion over the last year. Only Microsoft reported positive free cash flow in the third quarter. Looking ahead, the strategists estimate these four companies plan to spend another $232 billion on capex in the fourth quarter.

The AI trade saw a serious slamming on Friday, with more than $1 trillion in market value wiped away as investors fretted about the weakening cash flow profiles of Big Tech.

"The AI narrative is cracking as profitability concerns intensify," warned Miller Tabak chief markets strategist Matt Maley.

Over the weekend, the FBI said the attack was linked to North Korea.

"The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is releasing information advising the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of more than $6 billion USD in virtual assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, on or about October 29, 2026," a press release said.

Customer withdrawals were temporarily suspended, and co-CEO Richard Teng promised the exchange will cover all losses.

Teng said the hack was not carried out by one person. Initial findings pointed to a compromised laptop, but further review revealed broader security breaches.

"This was a complex attack," Teng said. "The attacker also used a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and tracers."

Around $3.24 billion remains in addresses linked to the theft, according to Tom Robinson, chief scientist and co-founder at blockchain analytics company Elliptic.

The attack has rattled crypto markets, and bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) traded at around $77,700 on Monday. Meanwhile, the total crypto market has lost roughly 3% in value, or $80 billion, over the last seven days, according to CoinMarketCap data.

Other major crypto assets also tumbled after the hack, with ether ( ETH-USD ) dropping to roughly $2,200. Binance's native token, BNB ( BND-USD ), also fell.

articles.title: 'Energy security's future lies in clean energy': PM Modi says fossil fuel dependence disrupts global economy
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday said the future of energy security lies in clean energy, warning that continued dependence on fossil
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday said the future of energy security lies in clean energy, warning that continued dependence on fossil fuels could disrupt the global economy.Speaking at the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo (BRESE) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, PM Modi said recent global crises, from the Covid-19 pandemic to the conflict in West Asia, had shown how closely energy security is linked to economic stability.He said India's investments and initiatives over the past decade had helped the country avoid major economic disruptions.“This global crisis has given a clear message to every country that energy security is directly connected to economic security. And we all know that the future of energy security lies in clean energy,” PM Modi said, according to ANI.“If we continue to rely heavily on fossil fuels, then the global economy will continue to be disrupted. Because the stockpile of fossil fuels is limited in some regions, but the potential of renewable energy is unlimited. And every region, every country can take advantage of it,” he added.Highlighting India's progress in renewable energy, PM Modi said the country had achieved its Paris Agreement commitment of sourcing 50% of its installed power capacity from non-fossil fuel sources in 2025, five years ahead of the 2030 deadline.Non-fossil sources now account for more than half of India's installed power capacity, which has reached nearly 300 gigawatts (GW). The country is working towards its target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030.PM Modi said India aims to add another 500 GW of non-fossil capacity over the next 10 to 11 years.He also highlighted the progress of the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, launched in February 2024 with a target of covering one crore households. More than 65 lakh homes have been connected under the scheme, with beneficiaries seeing a 76% reduction in their electricity bills, he said.Under the PM-KUSUM scheme, solar installations are benefiting more than 30 lakh farmers, generating estimated annual savings of Rs 1 lakh per farmer. Solar systems installed at over 44,000 government buildings are also saving around Rs 700 crore annually, the Prime Minister said.PM Modi said India's clean energy plans extend beyond solar, wind, hydropower and nuclear energy, with a focus on expanding green hydrogen production.“Our clean energy ecosystem is not limited to hydro, solar, wind and nuclear. India is moving ahead on a mission to make a big leap in the field of green hydrogen. Under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, the goal is to produce 50 lakh tonnes of green hydrogen by the end of this decade,” he said.He also highlighted the expansion of India's power grid and green energy corridors, backed by a recent government investment decision of Rs 2 lakh crore.On domestic manufacturing, PM Modi said India's solar module production capacity had increased from 2 GW a decade ago to more than 200 GW, while solar cell manufacturing capacity had reached 40 GW.The Prime Minister said the renewable energy sector had attracted investments worth more than Rs 15 lakh crore, or USD 164 billion, over the past decade.“Over the past decade, the renewable energy sector has seen over Rs 15 lakh crore, or USD 164 billion, in investment. Since the ReInvest summit of the year 2024, in just two years, we have seen investments of around Rs 6 lakh crore, or over USD 63 billion. articles.title: Oil drops 6% as Iran signals openness to peace talks
articles.summary: By Alex Lawler LONDON, Nov 2 (Reuters) - Oil fell about 6% on Monday as talks between Iranian and Qatari officials on ending the US-Israeli war with Iran lif...
articles.body:
LONDON, Nov 2 (Reuters) - Oil fell about 6% on Monday as talks between Iranian and Qatari officials on ending the US-Israeli war with Iran lifted hopes for reduced Middle East ‌supply disruptions, while Iran's president said the supreme leader had granted the government "certain authorities" regarding peace ‌talks.

Iranian negotiators held days of talks with Qatari mediators aimed at ending the war with the United States, and a draft proposal is being ​circulated with a follow-up meeting possible, an official briefed on the talks said on Monday.

Brent crude futures fell $6.78, or 6.0%, to $106.65 a barrel by 1357 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was down $6.37, or 6.1%, at $97.75.

The contracts fell as low as $105.86 and $97.12, respectively, after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said that Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei had granted the government ‌certain authorities for peace talks, boosting expectations ⁠of a diplomatic breakthrough, analysts said.

Pezeshkian added Tehran "will try to resolve the problem with dialogue", without elaborating, according to state media.

Brent ended October at its highest in six months on ⁠concerns that the Middle East conflict could escalate again after Tuesday's US midterm elections.

"The oil market is still reacting with extreme sensitivity to every headline out of the Middle East," UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo said. "While fears of an imminent escalation pushed ​prices ​up last week, they have dropped sharply at the start ​of this week as diplomatic talks between the ‌US and Iran continue," he added.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on Sunday that the purpose of the talks was to continue consultations with the Qatari mediators, adding that Tehran was prepared for "both defence and diplomacy".

The talks followed a recent increase in attacks on oil tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, though there have also been signs of shipments rising from some major exporters.

Saudi Arabia's crude exports increased in October compared with September, two of three ship-tracking companies said, ‌despite attacks by Iran-aligned Yemeni Houthis on its energy infrastructure.

The outbreak ​of the Iran war at the end of February has depleted ​oil stocks. The world has drained nearly 1 ​billion barrels from inventories since the war disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, said ‌Sultan Al Jaber, chief executive of ADNOC, Abu Dhabi's ​state-owned oil company.

Oil could rise ​further, some analysts say. Goldman Sachs raised its price forecasts on Sunday owing to elevated supply risks and said Brent could jump to $140 in 2027 if Gulf oil output remains 3.5 million barrels per day below ​its 2025 average.

articles.title: US market correction nearing end, Morgan Stanley strategists say
articles.summary: Nov 2 (Reuters) - The US market correction that began in June is in its "final innings", Morgan Stanley strategists said on Monday, adding that the November...
articles.body:
Nov 2 (Reuters) - The US market correction that began in June is in its "final innings", Morgan Stanley strategists said on Monday, ‌adding that the November 3 midterm elections should help remove ‌a major market overhang.

"We expect near-term clearing events to provide an attractive opportunity to add ​risk to quality cyclicals that have de-rated as we head into 2027," strategists led by Michael Wilson, Morgan Stanley's chief US equity strategist, said.

• The S&P 500 is catching down to weaker market breadth, which is typically the ‌last stage of a slump, ⁠Wilson said, noting 60% of Russell 3000 stocks have already seen at least a 20% correction since June

• The ⁠risk of a correction led by AI company earnings has kept markets on the edge. Last month, the tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 shed trillions of dollars in ​market value ​and was on the brink of ​entering correction territory

• Large-cap stocks ‌have typically gained 15% in the six months following election results, they said, adding that a Democratic sweep is already priced-in by investors

• The bigger risk would be what comes after the vote, with the potential of renewed military escalation with Iran or new tariffs, Morgan Stanley said

• Recent ‌earnings reinforce signs that the market correction ​could be nearing its end

• "Investors are no ​longer overlooking FCF shortfalls as ​they often did earlier in the cycle, consistent with ‌a more typical mid- to late cycle ​environment where earnings ​durability and cash conversion matter more," Wilson said

• He does not expect the Federal Reserve to rush toward interest rate cuts or ​add support, relief could ‌come from the US Treasury spending down its cash pile, from ​about $1.05 trillion to about $850 billion by year-end

(Reporting by Kanchana Chakravarty ​in Bengaluru; Editing by Tasim Zahid)

articles.title: India moves to resolve Scotch tariff dispute, assures 75% duty on bulk imports: Report
articles.summary: The government has moved to resolve a dispute over Scotch whisky imports under the UK trade pact, assuring liquor companies that bulk shipments qualify
articles.body: The government has moved to resolve a dispute over Scotch whisky imports under the UK trade pact, assuring liquor companies that bulk shipments qualify for the reduced 75 percent import duty after tax officials questioned their eligibility for the concession.According to a Reuters report citing six people with direct knowledge of the matter, commerce ministry officials gave the assurance during a closed-door meeting with liquor industry executives on Monday, saying New Delhi would honour the trade agreement in letter and spirit.One government source said, "We are potentially moving towards a resolution. Bulk Scotch whisky imports are indeed part of concessions under the trade deal."A second source said commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal told attendees that necessary steps were being taken to address the issue "so that the duty concession on bulk Scotch whisky is not impaired".The dispute centres on the agreement to reduce import duty on Scotch whisky in India from 150 per cent to 75 percent under the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), which came into effect in July 2026. However, tax officials had told liquor companies that the reduced duty did not apply to Scotch imported in bulk containers.The disagreement is significant because around 80 percent of Scotch whisky shipped to India arrives in bulk rather than in finished bottles.These imports are used by Indian manufacturers to produce Indian-Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL) whisky by blending Scotch with other spirits and ingredients. The industry maintains that both bottled and bulk Scotch imports should qualify for the reduced tariff under the trade agreement.The dispute has affected major liquor companies, including Diageo and Pernod Ricard, as well as Indian manufacturers Radico Khaitan and Allied Blenders and Distillers. Tax officials searched the offices of several companies in recent days and questioned executives over the classification and eligibility of bulk Scotch imports.The issue has also drawn attention from Britain and Scotland. The British government said it was working with New Delhi to resolve the matter, while the Scottish government separately raised concerns over the treatment of bulk Scotch imports.Scotch exports to India were valued at $335 million in 2024, and the Scotch Whisky Association has projected that the trade agreement could increase exports by an additional $1.34 billion over five years.You use AI every day. articles.title: Marvell to purchase Lumentum for $115 billion in record-breaking tech deal
articles.summary: Marvell stock declined after the chip designer said it will purchase optical parts maker Lumentum in a $115 billion deal.
articles.body:
What happened: Marvell Technology ( MRVL ) shares fell more than 4% on Monday after the chip designer announced it will acquire optical component maker Lumentum ( LITE ) in a deal valued at $115 billion. The transaction would be the largest merger between two publicly traded companies on record. Lumentum shares also fell 10% following the announcement.

What's behind the move: The record breaking agreement is expected to expand the combined company's total addressable market to $550 billion, according to the announcment.

"AI infrastructure is undergoing a fundamental architectural shift toward optical connectivity, creating an opportunity that comes along once in a generation," Matt Murphy, chairman and CEO of Marvell, said on Monday.

Lumentum shares fell as investors weighed the implications of the all-stock acquisition, under which shareholders will receive Marvell shares rather than cash.

Lumentum shareholders will get 4.5 shares of Marvell stock for every Lumentum share they own. The agreement mplies an enterprise value of approximately $115 billion, or $1,132 per share, representing a 23.9% premium over Lumentum's Oct. 28 closing share price.

What else you need to know: The acquisition gives Marvell greater access to optical technologies and manufacturing capacity, which have become critical bottlenecks of the AI infrastructure build-out.

Lumentum makes lasers and other optical components as increasingly powerful AI systems require faster connections. Marvell, which competes with Broadcom ( AVGO ), designs high-speed infrastructure and custom chips that enable AI computers to communicate with one another.

Earlier this year, Marvell stock rallied sharply after AI chip heavyweight Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang described the chip designer as "the next trillion-dollar company."

The company joined the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) index in June. Marvell shares are up more than 120% year to date. Lumentum shares have rallied more than 100%.

articles.title: 'Will consider all': Sitharaman on FPIs' concerns over equity taxation
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Monday said the government would consider concerns raised by foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) over
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Monday said the government would consider concerns raised by foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) over India's capital gains tax structure, amid growing demands for a reduction in long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax on equities.Responding to a question on whether the upcoming Budget would create a more favourable environment for foreign investors and encourage dollar investments, Sitharaman acknowledged the concerns of both retail investors and participants in the equity market.She said taxation was only one of several factors influencing investment decisions.“Taxation is just one part of it, but I quite appreciate and also realise the sensitivity and the anxiety which is prevailing among retail investors and also among equity participants,” she said at the Financial Express Leadership Awards 2026.The finance minister pointed out that India's tax structure was similar in 2023-24, when the country recorded its highest foreign investment inflows. However, she acknowledged that market conditions had changed since then, with net outflows by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) rising before showing signs of recovery.“The taxation structure was what it is today, even in 2023-24, when we had good inflow into the country. 23-24 saw the highest. The taxation was similar even then. Nothing differently was done for drawing investments. But of course, the situation is very different now. Circumstances have changed. Challenges have grown. More net FII outflows have happened. It's started resuming now. They've started coming back now. So I know that circumstances have changed and therefore voices of concern are louder. I quite appreciate that. I'll consider all this,” Sitharaman said.She added that India needed capital to sustain economic growth of over 7%, and acknowledged that investors' concerns needed to be heard.“Because at a time where our growth is very important, where people are putting their very best, that we are able to see sustained seven-plus growth. In order to keep that intact, we need capital... I wouldn't want to say more at this stage, but I recognise the voice,” she said.Sitharaman also highlighted the government's efforts to deepen and widen the bond market, while acknowledging that investors were seeking greater support for equity markets.Her remarks come amid growing calls for a review of the LTCG tax regime. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has reportedly recommended tax relief for both foreign and domestic investors.According to a Reuters report, SEBI has asked the government to consider scrapping LTCG tax on equity investments by foreign investors. It has also reportedly proposed tax relief for domestic mutual fund investors switching from one scheme to another.Under the reported proposal, investors would not have to pay LTCG tax when transferring their existing mutual fund investments to other schemes. articles.title: Apple has turned into Wall Street's hedge against the AI trade: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: Apple has become Wall Street's go-to hiding spot during AI selloffs, but memory costs could test its margins when it reports Monday.
articles.body:
When AI stocks get hit, investors have found a place to hide. It's the company that has mostly sat out the AI spending race — Apple ( AAPL ).

Chip stocks have had plenty of rough days this year, and Apple has mostly shrugged them off. On the 46 days the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) fell 2% or more, Apple rose on 30, about two out of every three.

That's new. From 1994 through last year, Apple rose on only about 1 in 6 of those days, and no year came anywhere close to this one, by Yahoo Finance's calculations.

Apple and chip stocks have basically stopped moving together. Apple's correlation with the chip index — a measure of how closely two assets move in step — turned negative in July and hit its lowest level on record in September.

The payoff showed up Friday. Over the past month, Apple gained about 3% while the iShares Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) tumbled about 17%. That gap pushed Apple back past Nvidia ( NVDA ) as Wall Street's most valuable company Friday.

It isn't just a one-month thing, either. Apple is up about 27% this year, more than double the S&P 500's ( ^GSPC ) gain.

Over their past four reported quarters, Amazon ( AMZN ), Alphabet ( GOOGL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), and Meta ( META ) spent more than $600 billion on capital expenditures — the money companies invest in long-lasting assets like data centers and chips — much of it to build out artificial intelligence. Apple spent about $10 billion.

Investors have started to sweat that bill. Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta all just reported negative free cash flow , meaning they spent more than their businesses brought in. Amazon's cash burn hit a record , and Alphabet's stock just wrapped up its worst month ever . No wonder investors have been rushing into Apple's AI-light arms .

Friday was chip stocks' worst day since June, and Apple still fell about 1%.

Apple can't fully escape the AI boom, either. It's paying more for memory chips, the same parts AI data centers are snapping up. Bank of America's Wamsi Mohan estimated those costs will take a real bite out of iPhone profit margins, and he thinks Wall Street's margin forecasts are too high into next year.

"Our estimates are below Street heading into earnings," BofA wrote in a note on Friday that kept a Buy rating on the stock.

Apple reports its fiscal fourth quarter results after the bell Monday, with iPhone 18 sales in the spotlight . Its outlook for December quarter margins will show whether the market's favorite AI hedge has an AI problem of its own.

articles.title: Anthropic reveals amended S-1 outlining huge spending commitments, rising sales
articles.summary: Anthropic has released its amended S-1, outlining rising sales and massive spending commitments.
articles.body:
Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) released an amended S-1 investor prospectus on Monday, updating its total revenue and spending through the first nine months of the year, showing increased sales and massive spending numbers.

The company said revenue grew $1,026% to $33.2 billion through the first nine months of the year that ended Sept. 30.

The original S-1 , which covered the first six months of the year through June 30, listed revenue of $16.2 billion. Anthropic recorded revenue of $4.6 billion in all of 2025.

Operating losses also improved year over year to -$1.3 billion in the first nine months of 2026 from -$5.2 billion in the same period in 2025.

Anthropic reported an operating loss of $536 million in the September quarter, compared with operating income of $974 million in the June quarter.

The company says the decline is the result of a $5 billion charge for compute under short-term commitments, as well as $2 billion in non-cash charges from its donation matching program.

The AI giant also revealed a staggering aggregate committed spend of $895.4 billion , which it says is primarily related to compute and infrastructure. Some $447.5 billion of that will hit before Dec. 31, 2030, with the remainder coming between 2031 and 2045; $69.8 billion will be due over the next 12 months.

The company's market debut will test investors' appetite for a second public listing by a firm with an already massive valuation. SpaceX ( SPCX ) went public on June 12 at $150 per share and ended the day 20% higher.

Anthropic didn't appear to make many changes to its vast risks section, which outlines possible scenarios in which the company's AI could go out of control, causing damage that even the world's combined insurance industry may not be able to cover.

In an early September essay, CEO Dario Amodei called on the AI industry to slow the development of frontier AI models over fears that they could become too powerful for humans to control. The piece, coupled with statements by former and current researchers at AI companies, sent shockwaves through the industry and raised concerns that the technology could "kill all humans."

Experts dispute those claims, saying that the risks surrounding AI stem from basic cybersecurity protections and from preventing people and governments from using it for things like identity theft, discrimination, and labor displacement.

articles.title: Anthropic's new IPO filing puts its computing bill near $900 billion
articles.summary: Anthropic's new IPO filing puts its computing commitments at about $895 billion and shows third quarter results slipping back to an operating loss.
articles.body:
Anthropic's first operating profit lasted one quarter. Its computing bill, nearly $900 billion, is just getting started.

The maker of Claude ( ANTH.PVT ) put a total on that bill for the first time Monday. Its amended IPO filing lists about $895 billion of commitments, nearly all of it for computing and data centers. About $70 billion comes due within a year. The full bill is almost seven times the roughly $132 billion of cash and short-term investments Anthropic held at the end of September.

The filing also added third quarter results. Revenue jumped to about $17 billion from $11.6 billion in the second quarter. But Anthropic reported a $567 million operating loss , one quarter after its first operating profit of $974 million.

Anthropic books most of its computing 12 to 18 months ahead. When demand ran past that capacity last quarter, it bought $5 billion of short-term computing that "currently costs significantly more" than its long-term deals, the filing says. A $2 billion non-cash charge tied to a donation-matching program added to the loss.

Three days before the filing, Seaport Research Partners analyst Jay Goldberg warned on Yahoo Finance that the profits wouldn't last.

"They will be profitable probably in the next quarter or two. But then they're going to start going back into losses," he said.

Nearly $450 billion of the commitments come due by the end of 2030. Purchase commitments alone jumped to about $314 billion from $55 billion at the end of 2025. Broadcom (AVGO) tops the list with about $161 billion in equipment leases. Alphabet's ( GOOGL ) Google is next at about $121 billion, up from $114.5 billion in the first filing. SpaceX's ( SPCX ) AI unit follows at up to $120.5 billion, then Amazon ( AMZN ) at $110 billion.

Anthropic also plans another $125 billion to $150 billion of Google chips and expects to spend more than $20 billion with AMD (AMD). Neither deal has a fixed dollar commitment, so neither counts toward the $895 billion.

That makes Anthropic one of the biggest customers the cloud giants have, and one of their rivals too.

"For the hyperscalers, Anthropic is at once a customer, competitor, sales channel and investment," Evercore ISI analyst Mark Mahaney wrote after the first filing.

Up to 7% of sales came from rule-breakers

Anthropic estimates that 5% to 7% of its revenue in the first nine months of the year came from customers who were breaking its usage policy or commercial terms. It stepped up enforcement in August and September and warned the crackdown "may reduce our overall revenue and growth rates in future periods."
